title: TwinVPN platform lifecycle CI evidence, version 1
description: What one platform link/run job MUST emit for its result to count as evidence. A job that cannot fill a field truthfully sets it false and states why in `notes`; it does NOT omit the field, because an absent field and a false one read identically in a summary and only one of them is honest. The First Implementation Wave criterion is that the shared core/platform boundary compiles, links, LOADS, INVOKES core code, RECEIVES a result back, and executes lifecycle state transitions -- so each of those is its own boolean and `verdict` is their conjunction, computed by build/acceptance/report.py rather than asserted by the job.

job_name.description: The stable GitHub Actions job name, so a reader can find the run that produced this.

runner.description: The pinned runner image or self-hosted label set, verbatim.

runner_kind.description: Hosted and self-hosted are DIFFERENT EVIDENCE and must not be conflated. A hosted simulator run never stands in for a privileged or physical-device run.

privileged.description: True only where the job actually exercised the privileged platform surface (WFP/driver/service activation, NetworkExtension activation, a physical device). A hosted smoke test sets this false.

toolchain.description: Whatever the job printed. Free-form on purpose: the rule is that versions are PRINTED and RECORDED, not that every platform names the same tools.

compiled.description: The shared core compiled for this target.

linked_real_core.description: The platform artifact linked the REAL shared-core artifact. A stub or a re-implementation is false.

loaded.description: The linked artifact loaded at runtime.

invoked_core.description: The test crossed the PRODUCTION FFI/native boundary and called TwinVPN core code.

received_result.description: A result came back THROUGH that production boundary.

lifecycle_transitions.description: Each transition actually driven and observed, as `FROM->TO`. An empty array fails the gate: a compilation-only job is insufficient.

test_command.description: The exact command whose exit status this evidence records.

artifacts.description: Paths uploaded for this job. MUST NOT name private device keys, pairing secrets, authentication tokens, tunnel plaintext, or unredacted packet captures.

notes.description: Required reading when any boolean above is false: say what did not happen and why.

verdict.description: PASS requires every boolean true AND at least one lifecycle transition. NOT-EXECUTED is for a job that did not run at all -- it is an ABSENCE of evidence and the gate treats it as failing, never as passing.
